If $\omega$ is the complex cube root of unity and $\left(\frac{a+b \omega+c \omega^2}{c+a \omega+b \omega^2}\right)^k+\left(\frac{a+b \omega+c \omega^2}{b+a \omega^2+c \omega}\right)^l=2$

$\frac{1}{x^4+x^2+1}=\frac{A x+B}{x^2+a x+1}+\frac{C x+D}{x^2-a x+1}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathbb{1}=(\mathrm{A} x+\mathrm{B})\left(x^2-a x+1\right)+(\mathrm{C} x+\mathrm{D})\left(x^2+a x+1\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathbb{1}=\mathrm{A}\left(x^3-a x^2+x\right)+\mathrm{B}\left(x^2-a x+1\right)+\mathrm{C}\left(x^3+a x^2+x\right)+\end{aligned}D\left(x^2+a x+1\right)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 1=(\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{C}) x^3+(-a \mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{C} a+\mathrm{D}) x^2+(\mathrm{A}-a \mathrm{~B}+\mathrm{C} \\ & +a \mathrm{D}) x+\mathbb{B}+\mathbb{D}\end{aligned}$
On comparing
$A+C=0$..(i)
$-a \mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}+\mathrm{Ca}+\mathrm{D}=0$...(ii)
$\mathrm{A}-a \mathrm{~B}+\mathrm{C}+a \mathrm{D}=0$...(iii)
$B+D=1$...(iv)
From (i), (iii)
$-a \mathrm{~B}+a \mathrm{D}=0$...(v)
From (iv) and (v) $; 2 a \mathrm{D}=a \Rightarrow \mathrm{D}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $\mathrm{B}=\frac{1}{2}$ From (iii) and (iv)
$-a \mathrm{~A}+a \mathrm{C}=-1$..(vi)
From (i) and (vi) $; 2 a \mathrm{C}=-1 ; \mathrm{C}=\frac{-1}{2 a}, \mathrm{~A}=\frac{-1}{2 a}\therefore \mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}=\frac{1}{2 a}+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{2 a}+\frac{1}{2}=1+\frac{1}{a}$
Now, comparing the denominator
$\begin{aligned} & x^4+x^2+1=\left(x^2-a x+1\right)\left(x^2+a x+1\right) \\ & =x^4+a x^3+x^2-a x^3-a^2 x^2-a x+x^2+a x+1 \\ & =x^4+\left(2-a^2\right) x^2+1\end{aligned}$
On comparing $x^2$ term
$\begin{aligned} & 2-a^2=1 \Rightarrow a^2=1 \Rightarrow a=1 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{~A}+\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}=1+\frac{1}{a}=1+1=2=2 a\end{aligned}$

questions.q: If $\int(\sqrt{\operatorname{cosec} x+1}) d x=k \tan ^{-1}(f(x))+c$, then $\frac{1}{k} f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=$
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}=\int \sqrt{\operatorname{cosec} x+1} d x \\ = & \int \sqrt{\frac{\tan ^2\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+1}{2 \tan \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)}+1} d x\end{aligned}\operatorname{Let} u=\tan \frac{x}{2} \Rightarrow d x=\frac{2}{u^2+1} d u\begin{aligned} \mathbb{I} & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{\sqrt{\frac{u^2+\mathbb{1}}{u}+2}}{u^2+1} d u \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{u+1}{\sqrt{u}\left(u^2+1\right)} d u\end{aligned}$
Let $v=\sqrt{u} \Rightarrow d v=\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{u}}\begin{aligned} I & =2 \sqrt{2} \int \frac{v^2+1}{v^4+1} d v \\ & =2 \sqrt{2} \int \frac{v^2+1}{\left(v^2-\sqrt{2} v+1\right)\left(v^2+\sqrt{2} v+1\right)} d v \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{v^2+\sqrt{2} v+1} d v+\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{v^2-\sqrt{2} v+1} d v \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(v+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}} d v+\sqrt{2} \int \frac{1}{\left(v-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}} d v\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} v+1)+2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} v-1) \\ & =2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} u+1)+2 \tan ^{-1}(\sqrt{2} u-1)\end{aligned}=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2} u}{1-u}\right)=2 \tan ^{-1}\left(\frac{\sqrt{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}}{1-\tan \frac{x}{2}}\right)\Rightarrow k=2, f(x)=\frac{\sqrt{2 \tan \frac{x}{2}}}{1-\tan \frac{x}{2}} \quad\left[\because \tan \frac{\pi}{12}=2-\sqrt{3}\right]\Rightarrow \frac{1}{k} f\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\sqrt{4-2 \sqrt{3}}}{1-(2-\sqrt{3})}=\frac{1}{2} \frac{\sqrt{(1-\sqrt{3})^2}}{\sqrt{3}-1}=\frac{-1}{2}$

$\begin{aligned} & (x+1+h)(x-1+2 \omega+h)\left(x-1+2 \omega^2+h\right)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow x^3+\left[3 h-1+2 \omega+2 \omega^2\right] x^2+\left[4+4 \omega^2 h+4 \omega h-2 \text { h }\right. \\ & \left.\quad+3 h^2-1\right] x+\text { constant term }=0\end{aligned}x^2$ and $x$ terms are missing
$\Rightarrow 3 h-1+2 \omega+2 \omega^2=0 \Rightarrow h=1$

questions.q: Two long straight parallel wires $A$ and $B$ separated by 5 m carry currents 2 A and 6 A respectively in the same direction. The resultant magnetic field due to the two wires at a point of 2 m distance from the wire $A$ in between the two wires is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_1=2 \mathrm{~A}, \mathrm{I}_2=6 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{r}_1=2 \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{r}_2=3 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$ The resultant magnetic field at point $P$ is $B=\frac{\mu_0}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{I_2}{r_2}-\frac{I_1}{r_1}\right)=2 \times 10^{-7}\left(\frac{6}{3}-\frac{2}{2}\right)=2 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~T}$

questions.q: A short bar magnet placed in a uniform magnetic field making an angle with the field experiences a torque. If the angle made by the magnet with field is changed from $30^{\circ}$ to $45^{\circ}$, the torque of the magnet
questions.solution: The torque on a bar magnet in magnetic field is $\tau=\mathrm{MB} \sin \theta_\alpha \sin \theta\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{\tau_2}{\tau_1}=\frac{\sin \theta_2}{\sin \theta_1}=\frac{\sin 45^{\circ}}{\sin 30^{\circ}}=\frac{1 / \sqrt{2}}{1 / 2}=\sqrt{2} \\ & \therefore \tau_2=1.414 \tau_1 \\ & \therefore \% \text { change in } \tau \\ & \Delta \tau \%=\frac{\tau_2-\tau_1}{\tau_1} \times 100=\frac{1.414 \tau_1-\tau_1}{\tau_1} \times 100 \\ & =41.4 \% \text { increases }\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A capacitor of capacitance $(4.0 \pm 0.2) \mu \mathrm{F}$ is charged to a potential of $(10.0 \pm 0.1) \mathrm{V}$. The charge on the capacitor is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C}=(4.0 \pm 0.2) \mu \mathrm{F}, \mathrm{V}=(10.0 \pm 0.1) \mathrm{V}$ The charge on capacitor is
$Q=C V=4 \times 10=40 \mu C$ Also, $\frac{\Delta \mathrm{Q}}{\mathrm{Q}}=\frac{\Delta \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{C}}+\frac{\Delta \mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{V}}=\frac{0.2}{4}+\frac{0.1}{10}=0.06\begin{aligned} & \therefore \% \Delta Q=\frac{\Delta Q}{Q} \times 100=0.06 \times 100=6 \% \\ & \therefore \quad \text { Charge, }(Q \pm \Delta Q \%)=40 \mu C \pm 6 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The work done in blowing a soap bubble of volume $V$ is $W$. The work done in blowing the bubble of volume $2 V$ from the same soap solution is
questions.solution:
Work done in blowing a soap bubble,
$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{T} \cdot \mathrm{A}=\mathrm{T}\left(4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2\right), \mathrm{W} \propto \mathrm{r}^2$
Also, Volume, $V=\frac{4}{3} \pi \mathrm{r}^3 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r} \propto \mathrm{V}^{1 / 3}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{W} \propto \mathrm{V}^{2 / 3} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{~W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{V}_2}{\mathrm{~V}_1}\right)^{2 / 3}=\left(\frac{2 \mathrm{~V}}{\mathrm{~V}}\right)^{2 / 3}=(2)^{2 / 3} \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{~W}_2=(2)^{2 / 3} \mathrm{~W}_1=(4)^{1 / 3} \mathrm{~W}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The power of a thin convex lens placed in air is +4 D . The refractive index of the material of the convex lens is $\frac{3}{2}$. If this convex lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $\frac{5}{3}$, then
options: it behaves like a convex lens of focal length 75 cm
it behaves like a convex lens of focal length 125 cm
it behaves like a concave lens of focal length 125 cm
it behaves like a concave lens of focal length 75 cm
questions.solution:
For thin convex lens, $P=+4 D, \mu_{\ell}=\frac{3}{2}, \mu_m=\frac{5}{3}\therefore P=\frac{1}{f_a} \Rightarrow f_a=\frac{1}{4} m=25 \mathrm{~cm}$
In air, $\frac{1}{f_a}=\left(\mu_{\ell}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{R_1}-\frac{1}{R_2}\right)$...(i) In medium, $\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}}=\left(\frac{\mu_{\ell}}{\mu_{\mathrm{m}}}-1\right)\left(\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{I}}}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{R}_2}\right)$.....(ii) Dividing eq (ii) by (i) $\frac{f_m}{f_a}=\frac{\left(\mu_{\ell}-1\right)}{\left(\frac{\mu_{\ell}}{\mu_m}-1\right)}=\frac{\left(\frac{3}{2}-1\right)}{\left(\frac{3 / 2}{5 / 3}-1\right)}=-5\therefore \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{m}}=-5 \times \mathrm{f}_{\mathrm{a}}=-5 \times 25=-125 \mathrm{~cm}$
$\therefore$ The lens behaves like a concave lens of focal length 125 cm.

questions.q: A hollow cylinder and a solid cylinder initially at rest at the top of an inclined plane are rolling down without slipping. If the time taken by the hollow cylinder to reach the bottom of the inclined plane is 2 s , the time taken by the solid cylinder to reach the bottom of the inclined plane is
questions.solution:
For rolling on an inclined plane,
Time, $\mathrm{t}=\sqrt{\frac{21}{\mathrm{a}}}=\sqrt{\frac{21}{\mathrm{~g} \sin \theta}\left(1+\frac{\mathrm{K}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}\right)}\Rightarrow t \propto \sqrt{1+\frac{K^2}{R^2}}\therefore$ For hollow cylinder, $\frac{\mathrm{K}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_1 \propto \sqrt{2}$
For solid cylinder, $\frac{\mathrm{K}^2}{\mathrm{R}^2}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}_2 \propto \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\therefore \frac{t_2}{t_1}=\frac{\sqrt{3 / 2}}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow t_2=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} t_1=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 2=1.732 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.q: Steam of mass 60 g at a temperature $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is mixed with water of mass 360 g at a temperature $40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. The ratio of the masses of steam and water in equilibrium is (Latent heat of steam is $540 \mathrm{cal} \mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and specific heat capacity of water is $1 \mathrm{cal} \mathrm{g}^{-1}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
For water, $\mathrm{m}_1=360 \mathrm{~g}, \mathrm{~T}_1=40^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{T}_2=100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\therefore$ Heat required, $\mathrm{H}_1=\mathrm{m}_1 \mathrm{C}_1\left(\mathrm{~T}_2-\mathrm{T}_1\right)=360 \times 1 \times(100-40)=21600 \mathrm{cal}$ At equilibrium, Heat released by steam = Heat required by water $\therefore$ Mass of steam converted into water, $\mathrm{m}_2=\frac{\mathrm{H}_1}{\mathrm{~L}}=\frac{21600}{540}=40 \mathrm{~g}$
$\therefore$ Mass of steam let, $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}=60-40=20 \mathrm{~g}$ Mass of water, $m_w=360+40=400 \mathrm{~g}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{s}}}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{W}}}=\frac{20}{400}=1: 20$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The temperature difference between the ends of two cylindrical rods $A$ and $B$ of the same material is $2: 3$. In steady state the ratio of the rates of flow of heat through the rods $A$ and $B$ is $5: 9$. If the radii of the rods $A$ and $B$ are in the ratio $1: 2$, then the ratio of lengths of the rods $A$ and $B$ is
questions.solution:
For two cylindrical rods A and B, $\theta_1: \theta_2=2: 3, H_1: H_2=5: 9, r_1: r_2=1: 2\therefore \quad$ At steady state, $\mathrm{H}=\frac{\mathbb{k}\left(\pi \mathrm{r}^2\right)^8}{\ell} \propto \frac{\mathrm{r}^2 \theta}{\ell}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{H}_1}{\mathrm{H}_2}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{r}_1}{\mathrm{r}_2}\right)^2\left(\frac{\theta_1}{\theta_2}\right)\left(\frac{\ell_2}{\ell_1}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \frac{5}{9}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) \cdot\left(\frac{\ell_2}{\ell_1}\right) \Rightarrow \frac{\ell_1}{\ell_2}=3: 10$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When $Q_1$ amount of heat is supplied to a monatomic gas, the work done by the gas is $W$. When $Q_2$ amount of heat is supplied to a diatomic gas, the work done by the gas is $2 W$. Then $Q_1: Q_2=$
questions.solution:
At constant pressure,
$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{P} \Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathbf{n R} \Delta \mathrm{T} \Rightarrow \mathbf{W} \propto \Delta \mathrm{T}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{W}_2}{\mathrm{~W}_1}=\frac{(\Delta \mathrm{T})_2}{(\Delta \mathrm{~T})_1} \Rightarrow \frac{2 \mathrm{~W}}{\mathrm{~W}}=\frac{(\Delta \mathrm{T})_2}{(\Delta \mathrm{~T})_1} \\ & \therefore(\Delta \mathrm{~T})_2=2(\Delta \mathrm{~T})_1\end{aligned}$
For monoatomic gas, $f_1=3\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{Q}_1=(\Delta \mathrm{U})_1+\mathrm{W}_1=\frac{\mathrm{f}_1}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1+\mathrm{W} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{Q}_1=\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1+\mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1=\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1\end{aligned}$
For diatomic gas, $\mathrm{f}_2=5\begin{aligned} & \therefore Q_2=(\Delta U)_2+W_2=\frac{f_2}{2} n R(\Delta T)_2+2 W \\ & \Rightarrow Q_2=\frac{5}{2} n R \times 2(\Delta T)_1+2 n R(\Delta T)_1\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{Q}_2=\frac{14}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1 \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{Q}_1}{\mathrm{Q}_2}=\frac{\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1}{\frac{14}{2} \mathrm{nR}(\Delta \mathrm{T})_1}=5: 14\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of a bulb of power 60 W is $16 \%$. The peak value of the electric field produced by the electromagnetic radiation from the bulb at a distance of 2 m from the bulb is $\left(\frac{1}{4 \pi \epsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^2 \mathrm{C}^{-2}\right)$
questions.solution:
For electric bulb, $P=60 \mathrm{~W}, \eta=16 \%\therefore$ Intensity of bulb, $\mathrm{I}_B=\frac{P}{4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2}\therefore \quad P=\frac{60}{4 \pi \times(2)^2}=\frac{15}{4 \pi}$
Intensity of radiation, $I_R=\frac{1}{2} \mathbb{C} \varepsilon_0 E_0^2\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \eta \times \mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{B}}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{C} \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{E}_0^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 0.16 \times \frac{15}{4 \pi}=\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 10^8 \times \varepsilon_0 \mathrm{E}_0^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_0^2=\left(\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}\right)\left(\frac{0.16 \times 30}{3 \times 10^8}\right) \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_0^2=9 \times 10^9 \times 0.16 \times 10^{-7}=144 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{E}_0=12 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The path difference between two particles of a sound wave is 50 cm and the phase difference between them is $1.8 \pi$. If the speed of sound in air is $340 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$, the frequency of the sound wave is
questions.solution: For sound wave, $\Delta x=50 \mathrm{~cm}, \Delta \phi=1.8 \pi\therefore$ Path difference, $\Delta x=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \cdot \Delta \phi\Rightarrow \quad 50=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \times 1.8 \pi \therefore \lambda=\frac{500}{9} \mathrm{~cm}\therefore \quad$ Frequency, $f=\frac{v}{\lambda}=\frac{340 \times 9}{500 \times 10^{-2}}=612 \mathrm{~Hz}$

questions.q: A source at rest emits sound waves of frequency 102 Hz . Two observers are moving away from the source of sound in opposite directions each with a speed of $10 \%$ of the speed of sound. The ratio of the frequencies of sound heard by the observers is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{v}_{0_1}=v_{0_2}=10 \%$ of $v=\frac{v}{10}\hat{f}=102 \mathrm{~Hz}$
For observer 1, $\mathbb{f}_1=\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}-v_{0 \mathrm{I}}}{v}\right) f=\left(\frac{v-\frac{v}{10}}{v}\right) f=\frac{9}{10} f$ For observer 2, $f_2=\left(\frac{v-v_{02}}{v}\right) f=\frac{9}{10} f\therefore \frac{\mathrm{f}_1}{\mathrm{f}_2}=\frac{9 \mathrm{f} / 10}{9 \mathrm{f} / 10}=1: 1$

questions.q: The kinetic energy of a body of mass 4 kg moving with a velocity of $(2 \hat{i}-4 \hat{j}-\hat{k}) \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{m}=4 \mathrm{~kg}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}=(2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathrm{k}}) \mathrm{ms}^{-1} \\ \therefore & \mathrm{v}=|2 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}-\hat{\mathbb{k}}|=\sqrt{(2)^2+(-4)^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{21} \\ \therefore & \mathrm{~K} \cdot \mathrm{E}_0=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mv}^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 21=42 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A proton and an ' $\alpha$ ' particle are both accelerated from rest in a uniform electric field. The ratio of works done by the electric field on the proton and the $\alpha$-particle in a given time is
questions.solution:
Acceleration of charge particle in an electric field is
$a=\frac{q^E}{m} \therefore v=u+a t=\left(\frac{q^E}{m}\right) t \Rightarrow v \propto \frac{G}{m}\therefore$ Work done by electric field,
$\mathrm{W}=\Delta \mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mb}^2 \Rightarrow \mathrm{~W} \propto \mathrm{mv}^2 \propto \mathrm{~m}\left(\frac{\mathrm{q}}{\mathrm{m}}\right)^2\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{W} \propto \frac{\mathrm{q}^2}{\mathrm{~m}} \\ & \therefore \frac{\mathbb{W}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{W}_\alpha}=\left(\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{p}}}{q_\alpha}\right)^2\left(\frac{\mathrm{~m}_\alpha}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}\right)=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2\left(\frac{4}{1}\right)=1: 1\end{aligned}$
